metadata.title: European Court Performance Observatory — Cleaned Dataset (v1)
sources: CEPEJ study (via 2026 EU Justice Scoreboard Figures 1-5, 7, 9-14)
Eurostat gov_10a_exp COFOG99 Law Courts (via 2026 EU Justice Scoreboard Figures 33-34)

EL.name: Greece
EL.funding_tier: Moderate-to-Low per Capita / Major RRF Reformer
EL.role: Primary focus country: recovering from prolonged backlog with RRF-backed judicial map & digitization reforms
caveats: Methodology break (*) flagged in CEPEJ/EUJS series across civil/commercial and administrative figures.
Missing observations (NaN) in 2014, 2016, 2019, 2020 for All Non-Criminal; 2014 & 2019 for Administrative; and 2020 for Litigious Civil & Commercial.

IT.name: Italy
IT.funding_tier: High per Capita / Major RRF Reformer
IT.role: Large-budget Southern civil-law peer: significant RRF targets on disposition time reduction
caveats: 2020 COVID-19 court suspension spike visible in Disposition Time (673.9 days in Litigious Civil & Commercial).
High non-litigious civil volume inflates All Non-Criminal incoming caseload (5.55 per 100 in 2024 vs. 2.33 Litigious).

RO.name: Romania
RO.funding_tier: Low per Capita / High % of GDP Effort
RO.role: High-caseload Eastern EU benchmark: tests whether high GDP budget share offsets surging civil demand
caveats: Highest incoming litigious civil & commercial caseload among peers (8.42 per 100 inhabitants in 2024), yet maintains low disposition time (179.8 days).
Highest judicial expenditure as % of GDP (0.41% in 2024) despite lower EUR per inhabitant (76.08 EUR) due to GDP denominator.

SE.name: Sweden
SE.funding_tier: High per Capita / Lean Budget Share of GDP
SE.role: Upper efficiency frontier: high per-inhabitant funding (137.05 EUR) & digitalized courts with low civil litigation volume
caveats: Administrative incoming caseload (1.64 per 100 in 2024) is over double its litigious civil & commercial caseload (0.70 per 100), reflecting Sweden's broad administrative court remit (tax, social insurance, migration).
